simple: the number that identifies one participant in a group that communicates.
analogy: the number painted on each kitchen hall's door.
precise: an integer from 0 to N−1 identifying one process (or GPU) within a communicator; collectives are defined in terms of ranks.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the named group of participants that take part in a collective together.
analogy: the list of halls that share one delivery round.
precise: an object describing an ordered group of ranks and a private communication context; every collective is called on a communicator by all of its ranks (MPI_Comm in MPI, ncclComm_t in NCCL).
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one operation that all members of a group call together, such as summing everyone's numbers.
analogy: every hall passes bowls around the same table at the same time.
precise: a communication operation that every rank of a communicator must call, with matching arguments and in the same order as the other collectives; it completes only with everyone's participation.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one participant's data are copied to everyone.
analogy: the head of hall 0 sends the same recipe card to every hall.
precise: a collective after which every rank's buffer equals the root rank's buffer.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: everyone's numbers are combined (for example summed), and one participant gets the result.
analogy: every hall's tasting score is added up on the head chef's slate.
precise: a collective that combines the ranks' buffers element by element with an operation such as sum or max and leaves the result on the root rank only.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: everyone's numbers are combined, and everyone gets the result.
analogy: every hall ends up with the same total of all halls' scores.
precise: a collective that combines the ranks' buffers element by element and leaves the full result on every rank; equivalent to reduce-scatter followed by all-gather.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: everyone's numbers are combined, and each participant gets one part of the result.
analogy: each hall ends up with the finished total for one part of the menu.
precise: a collective that reduces the ranks' buffers element by element and leaves segment r of the result on rank r.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each participant has one piece, and afterwards everyone has all pieces.
analogy: every hall copies every other hall's finished page into its own book.
precise: a collective in which rank r contributes segment r and every rank receives the concatenation of all segments.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each participant sends a different piece to every other participant.
analogy: every hall sends each other hall the ingredients meant for that hall.
precise: a collective in which rank i sends its block j to rank j and receives block i from every rank: a transpose of blocks across ranks.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the one participant that is the source or the destination in a collective.
analogy: the head hall that sends out or collects the cards.
precise: the rank named in a rooted collective (broadcast, reduce, gather, scatter) as the source of the data or the receiver of the result; all ranks must name the same root.
source: D3 of F8-01 (MPI Forum, "MPI: A Message-Passing Interface Standard") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one turn in which every participant sends and receives at most once.
analogy: one pass of bowls around the table.
precise: a step of a collective algorithm in which each rank exchanges at most one message per link; the number of rounds multiplies the start-up cost alpha.
source: D5 of F8-02 (Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an all-reduce in which everyone only talks to their two neighbours in a circle.
analogy: passing bowls around a round table: add what comes from the left, pass it to the right.
precise: an all-reduce made of a reduce-scatter and an all-gather on a ring, each of N−1 steps of one segment of 1/N of the data; each rank sends 2(N−1)/N of the buffer, which is bandwidth-optimal.
source: D4 of F8-02 (Patarasuk and Yuan, "Bandwidth Optimal All-reduce Algorithms for Clusters of Workstations") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a segment is one participant's share of the buffer; a chunk is a smaller piece sent on its own.
analogy: a segment is one course of the menu; a chunk is one ladle of it.
precise: in a ring of N ranks the buffer is cut into N segments; segments are cut into chunks so that sending, receiving and reducing can be pipelined.
source: D4 of F8-02 (Patarasuk and Yuan, "Bandwidth Optimal All-reduce Algorithms for Clusters of Workstations") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: in each round, everyone exchanges everything with a partner twice as far away as last time.
analogy: halls pair up, swap full pots, then pair with halls twice as far away.
precise: an all-reduce (or all-gather) in log2 N rounds in which rank r exchanges its whole buffer with rank r XOR 2^k in round k; latency-optimal, but each rank sends log2 N full buffers.
source: D5 of F8-02 (Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: first halve the data in each round while combining, then double it back.
analogy: swap half a pot with a far hall, then a quarter with a nearer one, then hand the finished parts back.
precise: an all-reduce made of a reduce-scatter by recursive halving and an all-gather by recursive doubling: 2 log2 N rounds and about 2(N−1)/N of the buffer sent per rank.
source: D5 of F8-02 (Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a tree in which, each round, everyone who already has the data passes it to one more participant.
analogy: one hall tells another, then both tell one more each, and so on.
precise: a tree on N ranks in which the number of informed ranks doubles each round, reaching all ranks in ceil(log2 N) rounds; used for broadcast and reduce.
source: D5 of F8-02 (Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: sending no more data per participant than any all-reduce must.
analogy: no hall carries more bowls than the job strictly needs.
precise: an all-reduce in which each rank sends (and receives) 2(N−1)/N times the buffer size, the lower bound for all-reduce on N ranks; the ring and Rabenseifner's algorithm meet it.
source: D4 of F8-02 (Patarasuk and Yuan, "Bandwidth Optimal All-reduce Algorithms for Clusters of Workstations") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the message size divided by the time the operation took.
analogy: pots of soup delivered per hour, counted once per pot.
precise: S / t for a collective on a buffer of S bytes taking time t; it is not comparable between collectives or rank counts.
source: D6 of F8-03 (NVIDIA nccl-tests performance notes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: algorithm bandwidth corrected so it can be compared with the speed of one link.
analogy: the delivery rate of the busiest road, whatever the menu.
precise: algbw multiplied by a factor that depends on the collective and N; for all-reduce the factor is 2(N−1)/N, so busbw approaches the per-link bandwidth for a bandwidth-optimal algorithm at large sizes.
source: D6 of F8-03 (NVIDIA nccl-tests performance notes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the message size at which you reach half of the best bandwidth.
analogy: the pot size at which the cart is half as useful as with a full load.
precise: the size n_1/2 at which start-up time equals transfer time in the alpha-beta model (n_1/2 = alpha × beta for one message), so achieved bandwidth is half of the asymptotic bandwidth.
source: D5 of F8-02 (Thakur, Rabenseifner, Gropp, "Optimization of Collective Communication Operations in MPICH") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two participants send a message back and forth and time it.
analogy: two halls passing one bowl back and forth with a stopwatch.
precise: a point-to-point benchmark in which rank 0 sends n bytes to rank 1, which sends them back; half the round-trip time over many repetitions and sizes is fitted to alpha + n/beta.
source: R2 of F8-03 (run in this build, Open MPI 4.1.6)

simple: the map of which parts of a computer are connected to which, and by what kind of link.
analogy: the map of passages, corridors and the courtyard bridge between the halls.
precise: the graph of devices (CPUs, root complexes, PCIe switches, GPUs, NICs) and links (PCIe, CPU-to-CPU, GPU-to-GPU) of a machine; the path between two GPUs and its narrowest link set their peer bandwidth.
source: D9 of F8-04 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a box that splits one PCIe connection into several.
analogy: a junction where two halls' corridors join before the central hall.
precise: a PCIe device with one upstream port and several downstream ports; traffic between two of its downstream devices can be routed inside the switch without crossing its upstream link.
source: D9 of F8-04 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Root complex, root port, switch, endpoint

simple: a table with one row and one column per GPU, saying how each pair is connected.
analogy: the campus map turned into a distance table.
precise: for every GPU pair, the class of the path between them (direct link, same PCIe switch, through a root complex, across CPU sockets) and, in a measured matrix, its bandwidth and latency; vendor tools print one in their own notation.
source: R1 of F8-04 (run of the university's topology model in this build); vendor tools' notation not verified

simple: the order in which the GPUs pass data around the ring.
analogy: the seating order at the round table.
precise: a cyclic permutation of the ranks; the paths of its hops, and the links they share, set the ring's bandwidth.
source: R1 of F8-04 (run of the university's topology model in this build)

simple: starting the next piece before the previous one is completely done everywhere.
analogy: while your neighbour adds the first bowl, you already fill the second.
precise: overlapping the transfer of chunk k+1 with the reduction of chunk k (and with transfers on other hops), so the per-step time approaches the larger of transfer and reduce time instead of their sum; each chunk adds its own start-up cost.
source: D4 of F8-02 (Patarasuk and Yuan, "Bandwidth Optimal All-reduce Algorithms for Clusters of Workstations") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the sender waits when the receiver has no room.
analogy: never more than two bowls waiting on your side of the table.
precise: a bound on the data in flight between two parties, enforced by the receiver's free buffer slots or credits.
source: R1 of F8-05 (run in this build)

simple: a marker in a GPU's work queue that other queues can wait for.
analogy: a bell rung when a bowl has been delivered.
precise: a CUDA or HIP event recorded on a stream completes when all work before it on that stream has completed; cudaStreamWaitEvent makes another stream, possibly on another device, wait for it without blocking the host.
source: H1 of F8-05 (CUDA 12.0 cuda_runtime_api.h as installed, read in this build)

simple: several workers train the same model, each on a different part of every batch, and combine their results after every step.
analogy: four halls tasting different bowls of the same recipe and pooling notes.
precise: each of N workers holds a full copy of the parameters, computes the gradient of the loss on its shard of the global batch, and an all-reduce combines the gradients so every worker applies the same update.
source: D8 of F8-06 (Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one worker's copy of the model's parameters.
analogy: one hall's copy of the recipe.
precise: the parameters held by one data-parallel worker; correct data parallelism keeps all replicas identical after every step.
source: R1 of F8-06 (run in this build)

simple: all the examples used for one step, and each worker's part of them.
analogy: the 64 bowls of a night, and each hall's 16.
precise: the global batch size B sets the effective batch of the update; with N workers each processes a shard of about B/N examples, and gradients are divided by B (not by the shard size) before they are summed.
source: R1 of F8-06 (run in this build)

simple: sending gradients in a few large groups instead of one tensor at a time.
analogy: collecting notes into a few big envelopes before sending them round.
precise: packing many parameter gradients into buckets that are all-reduced as single messages, paying the start-up cost a few times per step and starting each bucket's all-reduce as soon as its gradients are ready, to overlap with the backward pass.
source: D8 of F8-06 (Li et al., "PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much of the ideal N-times speed-up you actually got.
analogy: four halls should do four nights' tasting in one night; did they?
precise: throughput with N workers divided by N times the throughput with 1 worker, for a stated weak-scaling (same per-worker batch) or strong-scaling (same global batch) setup.
source: C1 of F8-06 (Systems Curriculum milestone F3); a map, not a source

simple: telling the library that several calls belong together and should start as one.
analogy: one bell for several carts.
precise: the ncclGroupStart / ncclGroupEnd bracket, used when one thread issues collectives for several GPUs or fuses several operations; RCCL keeps the same names (not verified in this build).
source: D1 of F8-01 (NVIDIA, NCCL documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
